Controls the rendering of the editor label. Each __Item__ is a pattern that matches a file path. Both relative and absolute file paths are supported. The relative path must include the WORKSPACE_FOLDER (e.g `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/src/**.tsx` or `*/src/**.tsx`). Absolute patterns must start with a `/`. In case multiple patterns match, the longest matching path will be picked. Each __Value__ is the template for the rendered editor when the __Item__ matches. Variables are substituted based on the context:
- `${dirname}`: name of the folder in which the file is located (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> folder`).
- `${dirname(N)}`: name of the nth parent folder in which the file is located (e.g. `N=2: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/static/folder/file.txt -> WORKSPACE_FOLDER`). Folders can be picked from the start of the path by using negative numbers (e.g. `N=-1: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> WORKSPACE_FOLDER`). If the __Item__ is an absolute pattern path, the first folder (`N=-1`) refers to the first folder in the absolute path, otherwise it corresponds to the workspace folder.
- `${filename}`: name of the file without the file extension (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> file`).
- `${extname}`: the file extension (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> txt`).
- `${extname(N)}`: the nth extension of the file separated by '.' (e.g. `N=2: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.ext1.ext2.ext3 -> ext1`). Extension can be picked from the start of the extension by using negative numbers (e.g. `N=-1: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.ext1.ext2.ext3 -> ext2`).

Example: `"**/static/**/*.html": "${filename} - ${dirname} (${extname})"` will render a file `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/static/folder/file.html` as `file - folder (html)`.

enumDescriptions: Show up to the 2 most recent external sessions updated in the last 7 days. At startup, external sessions older than the second-most-recently updated local session are hidden.
Show external sessions updated in the last 24 hours.
Show external sessions updated in the last 7 days.
Show external sessions updated in the last 30 days.

description: Controls whether opening an agent session, from the sessions list or a session link, shows it in an editor instead of the Chat view. Like opening a file, an editor that already shows the session is revealed, and a session shown in the Chat view moves into an editor.
Controls whether all dirty editors except untitled editors are saved before sending a chat message.
Enables automatically using the active editor as chat context for specified chat locations.

Controls whether the new implicit context flow is shown. In Ask and Edit modes, the context will automatically be included. When using an agent, context will be suggested as an attachment. Selections are always included as context.

When enabled, the active editor is automatically forwarded as context, even when it would otherwise only be suggested. Selections and explicitly attached files are always included regardless of this setting.

Note: this setting currently only applies to Agent Host sessions (such as Copilot).
Delay after which changes made by chat are automatically accepted. Values are in seconds, `0` means disabled and `100` seconds is the maximum.
Whether to show a confirmation before removing a request and its associated edits.
Whether to show a confirmation before retrying a request and its associated edits.
Controls whether the Explain button in the Chat panel and the Explain Changes context menu in the SCM view are shown. This is an experimental feature.
Controls whether the editor automatically reveals the next change after keeping or undoing a chat edit.

Controls whether selecting a file in the changed files list of a chat response opens it in a diff editor showing the changes made by chat, or in a regular editor. Holding `kbstyle(Alt)` while selecting the file opens it with the opposite behavior.

Show Agent Host session changes as a working set above the chat input instead of the Changes pill in the editor window. Use its context menu to enable or disable Keep and Undo in both the working set and the editor, or choose Show Pill to turn this setting off. View All Edits opens all changed files in a diff editor. Hosts without a session changeset keep the Changes pill. Local and other chat harnesses are unaffected.
Controls whether tips are shown above user messages in chat. New tips are added frequently, so this is a helpful way to stay up to date with the latest features.
Controls whether an animation is shown when clicking the thumbs up button on a chat response.
enumDescriptions: Shows a confetti burst animation around the thumbs up button.
Shows floating thumbs up icons rising from the button.
Shows expanding pulse rings from the button.
Shows radiant lines emanating from the button.

description: Enables chat participant autodetection for panel chat.
deprecation: This setting is deprecated. Please use `chat.detectParticipant.enabled` instead.

description: Enables incremental rendering with optional block-level animation when streaming chat responses.
Controls whether supported links in chat are rendered as rich links with live metadata. Enabling this may make authenticated requests to services such as GitHub.
Controls the animation style for incremental rendering.
enumDescriptions: Content fades in while rising upward.
Content fades in from a blurred state.
Content scales up from slightly smaller.
Content slides in from the left.
Content reveals top-to-bottom with a soft gradient edge.

description: Controls how content is buffered before rendering during incremental rendering. Lower buffering levels render faster but may show incomplete sentences or partially formed markdown.
enumDescriptions: Renders content immediately as tokens arrive.
Buffers content until a paragraph break before rendering.

description: Controls whether completed chat responses collapse intermediate work while keeping the final response visible.
Enables chat participant autodetection for panel chat.
Controls whether chat requests use experimental tree-based sticky scroll instead of the sticky prompt header.
Controls how file and symbol references are displayed in chat messages.
enumDescriptions: Display file and symbol references as boxed widgets with icons.
Display file and symbol references as simple blue links without icons.

description: Controls whether context attached to the chat input, such as files, folders, images, symbols, tools, and pull requests, is shown as pills inline with the prompt text at the position where it was added, instead of above the input. Each inline attachment behaves like a single character: move the cursor across it, select it, or delete it like text. Sent requests show the same pills inline. The prompt sent to the model mentions each pill by its attachment's name and location, and attaches each attachment once, however often it is mentioned.
Configure [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) to editors for opening files from chat (for example `"*.md": "vscode.markdown.preview.editor"`).
Controls whether a chat session should present the user with an OS notification when a confirmation or question needs attention. This includes a window badge as well as notification toast.
enumDescriptions: Never show OS notifications for confirmations.
Show OS notifications for confirmations when the window is not focused.
Always show OS notifications for confirmations, even when the window is focused.

description: Automatically skip question carousels by telling the agent that the user is not available and to use its best judgment. This is an advanced setting and can lead to unintended choices or actions based on incomplete context.

Enables **Advanced Autopilot**, a single switch that turns on all advanced Autopilot behaviors that delegate more of the loop to the agent. Currently, after each Autopilot turn a small, fast model evaluates whether your original request is complete; if not, Autopilot keeps working using that evaluation as guidance for the next turn, instead of relying on the agent to signal completion itself.

Controls the default permissions picker mode for new local chat sessions. You can still change the permission mode per session, and each session remembers the permission mode that was used. If your organization disables auto approval, new sessions use Default Permissions.
enumDescriptions: Start new chat sessions with Default Permissions.
Start new chat sessions in Bypass Approvals mode.
Start new chat sessions in Autopilot mode.

description: Controls the default configuration for new agent sessions (such as Copilot). You can still change the mode and approval behavior per session, and each session remembers what was used.

The default model for new chat conversations. Use "auto" to let Copilot pick a model, a model family name (such as "opus" or "gemini") to use the latest available model in that family, or a full model id. An organization-managed default takes precedence over your saved preference. You can still switch the model within a conversation; each new conversation starts at the effective default.

Global auto approve also known as "YOLO mode" disables manual approval completely for _all tools in all workspaces_, allowing the agent to act fully autonomously. This is extremely dangerous and is *never* recommended, even containerized environments like [Codespaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces) and [Dev Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers) have user keys forwarded into the container that could be compromised.

**This feature disables [critical security protections](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/security) and makes it much easier for an attacker to compromise the machine.**

Note: This setting only controls tool approval and does not prevent the agent from asking questions. To automatically answer agent questions, use the [`chat.autoReply`](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22chat.autoReply%22%5D) setting.

Enable session sync to GitHub.com. When enabled, Copilot session data is synced to your GitHub account for cross-device access and richer insights. Requires `#github.copilot.chat.localIndex.enabled#` to also be enabled.
Repository patterns to exclude from session sync. Use exact `owner/repo` names or glob patterns like `my-org/*`. Sessions from matching repositories will only be stored locally.

Controls whether edits made by the agent are automatically approved. The default is to approve all edits except those made to certain files which have the potential to cause immediate unintended side-effects, such as `**/.vscode/*.json`.

Set to `true` to automatically approve edits to matching files, `false` to always require explicit approval. The last pattern matching a given file will determine whether the edit is automatically approved.

Controls which URLs are automatically approved when requested by chat tools. Keys are URL patterns and values can be `true` to approve both requests and responses, `false` to deny, or an object with `approveRequest` and `approveResponse` properties for granular control.

Examples:
- `"https://example.com": true` - Approve all requests to example.com
- `"https://*.example.com": true` - Approve all requests to any subdomain of example.com
- `"https://example.com/api/*": { "approveRequest": true, "approveResponse": false }` - Approve requests but not responses for example.com/api paths

Controls which tools are eligible for automatic approval. Tools set to 'false' will always present a confirmation and will never offer the option to auto-approve. The default behavior (or setting a tool to 'true') may result in the tool offering auto-approval options.
Controls whether the artifacts view is available in chat.
Rules for extracting artifacts from tool results by MIME type. Maps MIME type patterns (e.g. 'image/*') to group configuration.
Rules for extracting artifacts from written files by file path pattern. Maps glob patterns to group configuration.
Rules for extracting artifacts from memory tool calls by memory file path pattern. Maps glob patterns to group configuration.
Controls whether the input of the chat should be restored when an undo request is made. The input will be filled with the text of the request that was restored.
Enables editing of requests in the chat. This allows you to change the request content and resubmit it to the model.
The number of characters a paste must exceed before it is added to the chat input as an attachment instead of being inserted inline. Set this to a very large number to always paste inline.
Show chat agent sessions when chat is empty or to the side when chat view is wide enough.
Controls the orientation of the chat agent sessions view when it is shown alongside the chat.
enumDescriptions: Display chat sessions vertically stacked above the chat input unless a chat session is visible.
Display chat sessions side by side if space is sufficient, otherwise fallback to stacked above the chat input unless a chat session is visible.

description: Show a progress badge on the chat view when an agent session is in progress that is opened in that view.
Controls the wording and icons used by actions that archive and unarchive chat sessions, as well as the label of the archived sessions section.
enumDescriptions: Use Archive, Archive All, Unarchive, and Unarchive All.
Use Mark as Done, Mark All as Done, Restore, and Restore All.

Show the handoff tip with an alternate description.
deprecation: Use chat.agentsWindowBanner.enabled instead.

description: Controls whether the Agents Window shows a tip about using `/btw` to ask side questions.

When enabled, Codex sessions opened from the regular workbench (sidebar chat) run inside the agent host process using the Codex App Server instead of the OpenAI extension. Only one Codex implementation surfaces per window. Requires `#chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled#`.
Show the context window usage indicator in the chat input.
Show request and completion timestamps. Hover over a completion timestamp to show the elapsed response time.

Show an animated gradient border around the chat input while the agent is working or thinking, instead of pinning persistent progress above the input when scrolling. When disabled, the indicator remains visible while scrolling if `#chat.persistentProgress#` is enabled. The border animation has no effect when reduced motion is enabled.

Keep a working progress indicator at the bottom until the response finishes, with a colored or monochrome Draw animation, or without an icon. The indicator reports running subagents and background commands from the current or earlier requests, even while the main response progresses. The default is Draw in all versions of VS Code. Experiments can override the default; an explicit setting takes precedence. Tool calls follow `#chat.persistentProgressVerbosity#`. Except in Conversation mode, reasoning is separated into collapsible previews that break the tool chain. Standalone tools retain their icons. Completed responses still follow `#chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses#`. This replaces inner working progress; terminal activity animations and rich subagent pills are unchanged. Changes apply immediately; reduced motion keeps the indicator visible without animation.
enumDescriptions: Keep the original thinking, tool, and working progress rendering without a persistent indicator or VS Code logo.
Tie the VS Code mark with fast parabolic ribbon motion, hold it, then unravel it before a brief rest.
Use the Draw animation with the same grayscale treatment as the VS Code icon in the Agents window. High contrast themes retain their contrast color.
Keep the same persistent progress text and tool rendering as Draw (Monochrome), but hide the VS Code icon.

description: Control tool call details when `#chat.persistentProgress#` is enabled. Compact is the default and collapses tool groups in place when thinking or response text resumes, or the response finishes. When Agent Host activity data is available, headers summarize up to three activity groups, prioritizing edits and commands, without language model requests. Remaining activity is counted as other steps. Failed, skipped, denied, and unfinished tool invocations remain explicit, including in the other-steps count. Completed shell invocations count as commands without tracking later background process status. Groups with no recognized activity or outcome use a step count. Expand a summary to inspect all its tool calls. Conversation collapses reasoning and tool calls between response text into one section that starts collapsed, names the current tool call, or the heading of the current reasoning summary (Thinking when the reasoning has no heading), while it runs, and shows a generated summary or Finished thinking once it finishes. Has no effect when persistent progress is Off. Changes apply immediately.
enumDescriptions: Keep tool calls in expanded, headerless chains without an internal scrolling limit.
Preview tool calls while they run, then collapse each group to a single expandable summary row when the response moves on.

Collapse reasoning and tool calls together into a single section that names the current tool call or reasoning heading while it runs, then shows a generated summary or Finished thinking once it finishes.

description: Enable state indicators around chat editor sessions that are in progress, need attention, or have an unvisited completion. Customize the borders with `chat.sessionStateIndicator.inProgressBorder`, `chat.sessionStateIndicator.needsInputBorder`, and `chat.sessionStateIndicator.unvisitedBorder` in `#workbench.colorCustomizations#`.
Controls whether a chat session should present the user with an OS notification when a response is received. This includes a window badge as well as notification toast.
enumDescriptions: Never show OS notifications for responses.
Show OS notifications for responses when the window is not focused.
Always show OS notifications for responses, even when the window is focused.

description: Enables checkpoints in chat. Checkpoints allow you to restore the chat to a previous state.
Controls whether to show chat checkpoint file changes.
Controls access to installed Model Context Protocol servers.
enumDescriptions: Allows access to MCP servers listed in the registry that VS Code is connected to.
Allow access to any installed MCP server.

enumDescriptions: Only automatically start new MCP servers that have never been run.
Automatically start new and outdated MCP servers that are not yet running.

description: Controls whether MCP servers can provide custom UI for tool invocations.
Controls behavior when multiple MCP servers are discovered with the same name. 'disable' disables lower-priority duplicates. 'suffix' appends numeric suffixes to disambiguate.
enumDescriptions: Disable lower-priority servers with duplicate names.
Append numeric suffixes to servers with duplicate names.

description: Configures which models are exposed to MCP servers for sampling (making model requests in the background). This setting can be edited in a graphical way under the `MCP: List Servers` command.
Enables NuGet packages for AI-assisted MCP server installation. Used to install MCP servers by name from the central registry for .NET packages (NuGet.org).
Enable using tools contributed by third-party extensions.
Enable agent plugin integration in chat.

Plugin directories to discover. Each key is a path that points directly to a plugin folder, and the value enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) it. Paths can be absolute, relative to the workspace root, or start with `~/` for the user's home directory.

Controls which [agent plugins](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-plugins) are enabled or disabled. Keys are plugin IDs in `<plugin>@<marketplace>` form (where marketplace is defined in `#chat.plugins.marketplaces#`); values enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) the plugin. Discovered alongside the path-keyed entries in `#chat.pluginLocations#`. When set by policy, entries are additive: plugins mapped to `true` are enabled in addition to the user's own plugins, and only plugins mapped to `false` are blocked from loading.

Plugin marketplaces to query. Entries may be GitHub shorthand (`owner/repo` or `owner/repo#ref`), direct Git repository URIs (`https://...git`, `ssh://...git`, or `git@host:path.git`, each optionally suffixed with `#ref`), or local repository URIs (`file:///...`). Equivalent GitHub shorthand and URI entries are deduplicated.
When enabled, agent mode can be activated from chat and tools in agentic contexts with side effects can be used.

When enabled, network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) is restricted according to `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains#` and `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains#`. Domain filtering is also applied to those tools when `#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#` is enabled.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

Allowed domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) when `#chat.agent.networkFilter#` is enabled. In Copilot Agent Host sessions with sandboxing (`#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`) enabled, also restricts the integrated browser when outbound network access (`#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork#`) is allowed; an empty allow list adds no sandbox restriction. This list does not enable outbound access. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`. Outside sandboxing, when both allowed and denied lists are empty, all domains are blocked. Denied domains (see `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains#`) take precedence.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

Denied domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) when `#chat.agent.networkFilter#` is enabled. Also applies to the integrated browser in sandboxed Copilot Agent Host sessions (`#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`); allowing outbound network access (`#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork#`) does not bypass this list. Takes precedence over `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains#`. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.
The default mode for new chat sessions. When empty, the chat view's default mode is used.
The default folder for archives and folders created by the Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs command. When empty or unavailable, the default file-dialog location is used.
Enable agent debug logging for agent host sessions: surface their debug events in the agent debug panel. Takes effect immediately; only sessions that run while this is enabled are captured.

Maximum number of debug events kept in memory per agent host session for the agent debug panel. Older events beyond this limit are dropped from the in-memory buffer, which also lowers the totals (such as token usage) shown in the panel overview.

When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions use the Agent Host terminal tool override instead of the SDK's default terminal behavior. Not supported on Windows, where sessions use the SDK's terminal and sandbox runtime.

When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions load your shell profile (`~/.bashrc` on macOS and Linux, PowerShell profiles on Windows) and activate the Python environment selected for the workspace before each shell command. Python activation requires the Python Environments extension with `#python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType#` set to `shellStartup`. Local windows only.
Controls the log level for the Copilot SDK runtime used by the local agent host. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client; active sessions are reloaded when next used.
enumDescriptions: Log informational messages. Running VS Code with trace logging still enables all Copilot SDK runtime diagnostics.
Log all Copilot SDK runtime diagnostics.

description: When enabled, Copilot Agent Host sessions using a supported Claude model can call the provider-native Advisor tool. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish.
When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions are offered the Copilot runtime's search subagent tool for codebase search. Applies to sessions when they launch or resume.

CAPI model ID to use for the search subagent in local Copilot Agent Host sessions when `#chat.copilot.searchSubagent.enabled#` is enabled. Empty uses the runtime default. An unavailable model makes the search tool unavailable. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish.

When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions can use the runtime's built-in Explore agent, independently of `#chat.copilot.searchSubagent.enabled#`. Applies to sessions when they launch or resume. Does not disable custom agents named Explore.

When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions opt into the Copilot runtime's execution subagent. The runtime's experiment assignments may override this default. When the runtime implementation is available, the extension-native execution tool is excluded from that session. This is independent of `#github.copilot.chat.executionSubagent.enabled#`, which controls the extension-native implementation. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot runtime after active turns finish.

Default model ID for the Copilot runtime's execution subagent. Empty inherits the parent session model. The runtime's experiment assignments may override this default. This does not affect the extension-native execution subagent's model. An unavailable model disables the runtime execution subagent. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot runtime after active turns finish.
When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions running a Claude Opus 4.8 model apply Opus 4.8-tuned system-prompt section overrides on top of the default system message.

When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions order the system prompt by how often each section changes, so sessions with the same tools and workspace can reuse each other's prompt cache. This moves per-session sections, such as the environment and session folder, to the end of the system prompt. Applies to new and resumed sessions.
When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions defer MCP and non-core VS Code tools behind a tool-search tool so the model discovers them on demand instead of loading every tool definition up front.
Minimum number of tools before MCP and external tools are deferred behind tool search. Set to 0 to always defer external tools. Only effective when tool search is enabled.
Controls whether Copilot Agent Host sessions, such as those in the Agents window, add a `Co-authored-by: Copilot` trailer to the commits they create. Takes effect when a session starts or resumes.
Maximum number of characters available for skill descriptions in the Copilot SDK system message.
When enabled, makes the HydraFusion model available to local Copilot Agent Host sessions. Changing this setting restarts the local Copilot runtime.
enumDescriptions: Make HydraFusion v2 available, which plans with per-step reasoning effort and a wider set of models.

Make HydraFusion v2 available and ask the service to keep reusing the previous turn's root model when it fits the next turn's workflow, which improves prompt cache reuse. Also applies to HydraFusion tiers that Auto offers.

description: Selects the model Copilot uses to generate and edit images, or turns image generation off. Each model lists its rates. Account access and tool permissions still apply, and choosing **Off** prevents future image tool calls.
enumDescriptions: Agents cannot generate or edit images.

Generate and edit images with **GPT Image 2.5 Flare** when it is available to your account. Prompts and selected images are sent to Flare.

**Preview rates (AI credits per 1 million tokens):**
- **Text tokens:** 500 input / 0 output
- **Image tokens:** 800 input / 3,000 output

These charges are in addition to the conversation model. Rates may change; these are token rates, not per-image prices.

description: Request a visible "Made with AI" label on images generated or edited by Copilot. Applies to new and existing Copilot sessions without enabling image generation. Labels are generated by the image model and are not guaranteed. Turning this off does not remove existing labels from input images.

deprecation: Use `#chat.copilot.imageGeneration.model#` instead.

description: When enabled, Copilot Agent Host sessions take Auto's tiers from the Copilot service, and those tiers decide how Auto is presented. When they include a Fusion tier the account can run, Auto is presented as Copilot Fusion, with HydraFusion and HydraFusion Max among its tiers. When they include none, Auto is offered with the service's tiers. When the service provides no tiers, Auto, HydraFusion, and HydraFusion Max are offered as separate models. When disabled, Auto and HydraFusion are offered as separate models, with HydraFusion controlled by `#chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled#`. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot runtime after active turns finish.

When enabled, offers on-device models to download and run on this device with llama.cpp. Offered only on devices with a GPU that has about 64 GB of memory or more. Changing this setting restarts the local Copilot runtime after active turns finish. Local models may not use the same safety filters as GitHub Copilot-provided models and may be more susceptible to malicious instructions, especially when actions are automatically approved.

When enabled, Auto can route turns to the active on-device model, with cloud fallback. Takes effect immediately. Local models may not use the same safety filters as GitHub Copilot-provided models and may be more susceptible to malicious instructions, especially when actions are automatically approved.
Absolute path to a `llama-server` executable for on-device models. VS Code doesn't install llama.cpp: install a build that supports your model, then set this to its `llama-server`.

When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions can store and recall [Copilot Memory](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory). Your [Copilot Memory settings on GitHub](https://github.com/settings/copilot/memory) and organization policies still apply. Applies to sessions created or resumed after the setting changes.

When enabled together with `#chat.copilot.memory.enabled#`, local Copilot Agent Host sessions store Copilot Memory in the repository's `.github/copilot-memories.jsonl` file instead of GitHub's cloud memory service. The file is part of the working tree, so commits made by the agent or the Agents window can include it. Requires a GitHub-hosted repository. **Note:** your Copilot Memory settings and organization policies on GitHub don't apply, and user-scoped memories are unavailable. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish.

Override Auto's "Optimize for" preference for evals and debugging. Accepts `efficiency`, `balance`, or `intelligence` in both Copilot Chat and Copilot SDK sessions; `fast` is extension-only. Set to `null` to clear.
Per-model overrides for Copilot Agent Host sessions. Use `*` to match every model. Supports model family, reasoning effort, tool filters, model capabilities, and YAML prompt overrides.

Controls when sign-in surfaces, such as the sign-in dialog and the welcome screen, offer "Continue with Microsoft". Always offer "Continue with Microsoft", without checking for a linked account.
Never offer "Continue with Microsoft", and never check for a linked account.

The language model id used to generate tool risk assessments. Should be a small, fast model.
Select the default language model to use for the Plan agent from the available providers.
Select the default language model to use for the Explore subagent from the available providers.

enumDescriptions: Use the default behavior for utility models

Controls whether to allow auto approval in the run in terminal tool.

A list of commands or regular expressions that control whether the run in terminal tool commands require explicit approval. These will be matched against the start of a command. A regular expression can be provided by wrapping the string in `/` characters followed by optional flags such as `i` for case-insensitivity.

Set to `true` to automatically approve commands, `false` to always require explicit approval or `null` to unset the value.

Note that these commands and regular expressions are evaluated for every _sub-command_ within the full _command line_, so `foo && bar` for example will need both `foo` and `bar` to match a `true` entry and must not match a `false` entry in order to auto approve. Inline commands such as `<(foo)` (process substitution) should also be detected.

An object can be used to match against the full command line instead of matching sub-commands and inline commands, for example `{ approve: false, matchCommandLine: true }`. In order to be auto approved _both_ the sub-command and command line must not be explicitly denied, then _either_ all sub-commands or command line needs to be approved.

Note that there's a default set of rules to allow and also deny commands. Consider setting `#chat.tools.terminal.ignoreDefaultAutoApproveRules#` to `true` to ignore all default rules to ensure there are no conflicts with your own rules. Do this at your own risk, the default denial rules are designed to protect you against running dangerous commands.

Examples:
|Value|Description|
|---|---|
| `"mkdir": true` | Allow all commands starting with `mkdir`
| `"npm run build": true` | Allow all commands starting with `npm run build`
| `"bin/test.sh": true` | Allow all commands that match the path `bin/test.sh` (`bin\test.sh`, `./bin/test.sh`, etc.)
| `"/^git (status\|show\\b.*)$/": true` | Allow `git status` and all commands starting with `git show`
| `"/^Get-ChildItem\\b/i": true` | will allow `Get-ChildItem` commands regardless of casing
| `"/.*/": true` | Allow all commands (denied commands still require approval)
| `"rm": false` | Require explicit approval for all commands starting with `rm`
| `"/\\.ps1/i": { approve: false, matchCommandLine: true }` | Require explicit approval for any _command line_ that contains `".ps1"` regardless of casing
| `"rm": null` | Unset the default `false` value for `rm`
